newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy will cut rates as economy grows - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy will cut rates as economy grows - Fazio.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Thursday he would relax his current tight monetary policy as the economy gradually gained strength.
But Fazio told a parliamentary budget commission that he did not want to push the economy. "Don't ask me to force the economy or drug it," he said.

Italy's gross domestic product (GDP) slipped 0.5 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of the year, but Fazio said he expected average GDP in 1997 to grow by between 1.0 - 1.2 percent. The government has forecast GDP growth of 1.2 percent.
Fazio added that he expected GDP growth in 1998 to be below the government's 2.0 percent target.

The central bank has been urged to cut its official discount rate in recent months as the economy slowed and inflation fell sharply. However Fazio is believed to be worried that inflation is falling primarily because of subdued demand. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
